Article Title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi

PM Modi stresses packaging, highlights traditional skills

Heval river rejuvenation , e-Sanjeevani consultations highlighted

PM calls 12-year journey of Mann Ki Baat a ‘pilgrimage’

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday urged people to prioritise products made by local artisans while shopping for festivals, saying their purchases would strengthen the ‘Vocal for Local’ campaign and help realise the vision of a self-reliant India.Addressing the 139th edition of his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat , PM Modi said the campaign was helping Indian products reach international markets, citing the export of makhana from Bihar to Greece and arhar dal from Karnataka to the Maldives.The prime minister noted that people typically purchase gifts and other items for their families and loved ones during festivals, and called on them to support local artisans through their shopping choices.“This time too, while shopping, please give priority to products made by local artisans. Your purchases will boost their enthusiasm,” he said.PM Modi said greater participation in the ‘Vocal for Local’ campaign would accelerate the progress towards a self-reliant India.“Therefore, I personally urge you to give priority and prominence to products crafted by local artisans,” he added.The prime minister also emphasised the importance of packaging in attracting consumers and helping products find a place in the market.“Often, when we see something in the market, good packaging makes us pick it up, and we want to learn more about the product. Understanding this, greater emphasis is now being laid on packaging,” he said.During the broadcast, PM Modi also highlighted efforts to revive traditional skills and farming practices, including an initiative to promote natural cotton cultivation in Punjab’s Malwa region.He said the organisation Kheti Virasat Mission had been working to revive organic farming and had launched an initiative called ‘Nav-Trinjan’ to encourage natural cotton farming.The initiative also started a weaving school a few years ago to pass the traditional skill on to younger generations.“You can imagine how great a help this is for the environment. Friends, a few years ago, 'Nav-Trinjan' also started a weaving school with the goal of passing on the skill of weaving to the new generation,” PM Modi said.PM Modi also spoke about efforts by residents and the local administration in Uttarakhand’s Tehri Garhwal district to revive the Heval river.He said the river’s water level had begun to fall some time ago, while natural water sources in the surrounding areas were drying up. In response, villagers and the administration launched conservation efforts that included rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and large-scale tree planting.“Today, these efforts have given the Heval river a new lease of life while also helping rejuvenate dozens of natural water sources,” the prime minister said.He also highlighted the use of technology in healthcare through the e-Sanjeevani telemedicine service, which enables people to access medical consultations remotely.“It brings me immense satisfaction to share that nearly 50 crore tele-consultations have been conducted through it so far. This is a massive figure and a prime example of the power of technology, the service-mindedness of our doctors, and the trust of our citizens,” he said.PM Modi added that the service’s extensive network enabled it to reach even the most remote parts of the country, with beneficiaries’ experiences offering examples of its reach.The Sunday broadcast also marked 12 years of Mann Ki Baat. PM Modi described the programme’s journey as a “pilgrimage”, saying it had allowed him to learn about citizens’ efforts and acknowledge their contributions.“Since then, our journey has been continuing without interruption. You are both fellow travellers and guides on this journey,” he said, recalling that the programme began on Vijayadashami 12 years ago.The prime minister said the broadcast had given him an opportunity to highlight the hard work, courage, dedication and spirit of service shown by ordinary people across the country.“For me, Mann Ki Baat is no less than a pilgrimage to closely learn about the efforts of the people of the country and to bow down to their contributions,” he said.PM Modi added that the programme had brought attention to people whose work might otherwise go unnoticed and had allowed him to connect with families across India.He said he received hundreds of messages from listeners who told him that listening to Mann Ki Baat made them feel as though he were sitting among them and speaking as a member of their family. He described the affection expressed by listeners as an “invaluable asset”.
Article Summary: PM Modi stresses packaging, highlights traditional skills and farming practices. Heval river rejuvenation, e-Sanjeevani consultations highlighted. PM calls 12-year journey of Mann Ki Baat a ‘pilgrimage’Join conversation. Share your thoughts in the comments.

Article Title: 'Now that Nitish is no longer there': Expelled Anant Singh says has no regrets, to float own party
Article Text:
‘No distance between me and Nitish’: Anant Singh after JD(U) expels him, wife

NEW DELHI: Expelled Janata Dal (United) strongman Anant Singh on Sunday claimed the Nitish Kumar 's party is “finished” after his expulsion, predicting that it would fail to win even 10 seats in the next election.The Mokama MLA and Nitish Kumar loyalist also said he had “no regrets” over the action and maintained that he shared a cordial relationship with Nitish Kumar.Anant Singh's remarks came a day after the JD(U), which has been in power in Bihar for nearly two decades under Nitish Kumar’s leadership, expelled him and his wife, Neelam Devi , for six years over alleged “anti-party” activities.Speaking to reporters, Singh said he would form his own political party and questioned the future of the JD(U) after Nitish Kumar’s exit from Bihar throne and move away from an active role in state politics.“The party belonged to Nitish Kumar. Now that Nitish Kumar is no longer there (in the active role), what is left of the party? Who among those in the leadership-- the ones who expelled me—has actually contributed anything?... Now, they will not even get 10 seats... Why will I go anywhere? I will simply build my own party,” he said.“The JD(U) is finished. Once they hold elections, everything will become clear,” Mokama MLA added.Despite his criticism of the party, Singh denied any rift with Nitish Kumar, saying, “There is no distance between me and Nitish-ji; we maintain a cordial relationship. I will go and visit him sometime -- there’s no issue. Let them keep their party; it serves no real purpose anyway.”“I will simply build my own party... I have no regrets. Whatever action has been taken, it’s fine; I have no issues with it,” he said.The JD(U) had accused Anant Singh of repeatedly disobeying the party leadership and using inappropriate and insulting language against its senior leaders.In a further move, the party has approached Bihar Legislative Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh’s disqualification as an MLA under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, commonly known as the anti-defection law.
Article Summary: Mokama MLA and Nitish Kumar loyalist Anant Singh said he would form his own political party. Singh's remarks came a day after the JD(U) expelled him and his wife, Neelam Devi, for six years over alleged “anti-party” activities.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday urged the United Nations to take a stronger leadership role in tackling global crises, saying it must not remain a spectator to conflicts and other challenges facing the world.Speaking at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan on the occasion of UN Day, Jaishankar called for reforms in multilateral institutions, arguing that large parts of the world could not be excluded from decision-making.“The UN must show leadership, not be a spectator to global crises,” he said, adding that the case for reformed multilateralism was growing stronger by the day.Jaishankar also described terrorism as a major threat to global peace, rejecting its use as an instrument of statecraft.“Its usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable. It can never be justified, it can never be rationalized,” he said, calling for stronger international resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms.The minister said some countries continued to allow political calculations to take precedence over the fight against terrorism, despite the lessons of history.Jaishankar highlighted the challenges confronting developing countries, describing the Global South as facing a “4F crisis” involving finance, fuel, food and fertiliser.He said developed countries also had a stake in finding solutions and called for urgent steps to reduce risks in the international economy and provide nations with more diversified options.“Market distortions through constriction and choke points only add to suffering. A genuine dialogue in this regard is overdue,” he said.On technological change, Jaishankar said artificial intelligence could transform the world but warned against leaving its development and impact in the hands of a few.“AI promises to be the mother of all change,” he said, arguing that such a far-reaching technology required a responsible, inclusive and human-centric approach.He said India supported a broader perspective on AI, given its universal applicability and potential consequences for societies worldwide.Jaishankar also stressed that progress and prosperity were inseparable, saying the world could not advance while large sections of humanity remained deprived.
Article Summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday urged the United Nations to take a stronger leadership role in tackling global crises. He said the Global South was facing a ‘4F crisis’ involving finance, fuel, food and fertiliser. He also called for multilateral reforms and inclusive AI development.

Article Title: Centre rushes 250 RAF personnel to Arunachal after violent protests over hydropower project
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Centre has sent two companies of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to Arunachal Pradesh following violence in Pasighat during protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, officials said on Sunday.The ministry of home affairs (MHA) directed on Saturday that the two companies, comprising around 250 personnel, be airlifted from Navi Mumbai aboard an Indian Air Force transport aircraft. The units are expected to reach Pasighat and be deployed by Sunday, officials told news agency PTI.The RAF is a specialised anti-riot unit of the CRPF whose personnel wear blue uniforms.Several CRPF units are already deployed in the violence-hit areas. Arunachal Pradesh also has a permanent deployment of around two to three CRPF battalions.Officials said CRPF personnel had effectively handled the protests since Friday and prevented the violence from escalating. Several police and central forces personnel were injured during the clashes, they added.On Friday night, a mob torched an NHPC office and a police station and vandalised the residences of three political leaders, including the state BJP president, in East Siang district, according to Arunachal Pradesh Police officials.Arunachal chief minister Pema Khandu said the right to peaceful protest was an essential part of democracy, but stressed that demonstrations must remain within the bounds of the law and should not lead to property damage or disruption of public order.Describing the incidents in Pasighat as regrettable, Khandu appealed to all sections of society to maintain peace.According to a statement issued by the chief minister's Office (CMO), a 12-hour bandh in Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts over the proposed power project remained largely peaceful on Friday. However, violence broke out in Pasighat after the bandh ended and continued until 3.30 am on Saturday.Protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) turned violent in Pasighat, East Siang district, on Friday night, with "Gen Z" protesters allegedly setting fire to the NHPC office and a police station and vandalising and looting the residences of two MLAs and the state BJP president, police said.The violence continued in waves for nearly nine hours into Saturday morning, leaving "over 40 police personnel injured in stone-pelting", police said. A protester was hit in the leg by a tear gas shell and admitted to hospital.Following the violence, the East Siang district administration imposed restrictions on public gatherings and processions in Pasighat, Mebo and Ruksin, citing fears of vandalism, arson and a possible breach of law and order amid protests and bandh-related activities.India’s proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, planned across three districts of Arunachal, is being pitched as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam upstream. But the plan has faced resistance from indigenous tribes, who fear the reservoir could submerge villages and sever their deep-rooted ties with the river.Known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, the Siang enters Arunachal Pradesh near Gelling and flows for 294km before meeting the Dibang and Lohit rivers at Sadiya in Assam to form the Brahmaputra.
Article Summary: The Centre has sent two companies of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to Arunachal Pradesh. The RAF is a specialised anti- riot unit of the CRPF whose personnel wear blue uniforms. Several police and central forces personnel were injured during the clashes.

Article Title: ‘Foreign-funded conspiracy to destabilise India’: Telangana BJP chief targets Congress over Jamia graffiti
Article Text:
Rao claimed that the opposition was encouraging students to act against national interests

Jamia protests trigger political row

NEW DELHI: Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao on Sunday accused the Congress and the INDIA alliance of encouraging anti-national activities, alleging that the controversy over graffiti at Delhi’s Jamia Millia Islamia was part of a broader conspiracy to destabilise the country.Speaking to ANI, Rao claimed that radical networks within student groups were being supported by opposition political parties. He also alleged that the campus demonstrations were part of a foreign-sponsored effort to create unrest in India, though he did not provide evidence to substantiate the claim.“Writing on the walls of Jamia Millia University in Delhi, all these things are now being exposed because there are people who are part of the ‘Tukde-Tukde’ gang and anti-national gangs who are among the students, and they are in support of Sharjeel Imam, who has actually been involved in several anti-national activities,” Rao said.Targeting the Congress and other INDIA alliance parties over their alleged silence on the controversy, Rao claimed that the opposition was encouraging students to act against national interests.“This slogan shows that the Congress and the INDIA alliance, which are silent on this issue, show how they are inciting students and everyone in the country to go against the interests of the nation and indulge in anti-national activities,” he said.Rao further alleged that the protests were designed to create anarchy and were being sponsored by a foreign country to destabilise India.The BJP leader’s remarks come amid heightened tensions at Jamia Millia Islamia, where university authorities recently shifted classes to an online format, citing student safety amid ongoing campus demonstrations.The controversy has also drawn Congress leaders into the dispute. Congress MP Imran Masood, who visited the university to meet protesting students on Friday, denied that slogans calling for a “free Kashmir” had been raised during the demonstrations. Delhi Police detained Masood during his visit.“No slogans calling for a ‘free Kashmir’ were raised there, not a single one. I stood up in front of everyone and strongly condemned such slogans, stating that Kashmir is an integral part of India,” Masood told ANI.Since Oct 12, students have been on a sit-in and hunger strike, which has grown into Jamia's biggest student protest since the anti-CAA agitation. Jamia has not had an elected union since 2006, when it was dissolved following violence. It is one of Delhi's few central universities without an elected union.
Article Summary: Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao accused the Congress and the INDIA alliance of encouraging anti-national activities. Rao claimed that radical networks within student groups were being supported by opposition political parties. He also alleged that the campus demonstrations were part of a foreign- sponsored effort to create unrest in India.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday took a swipe at BJP, thanking the ruling party and its allies for promoting the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, as he urged people to join the protest over alleged “vote chori”. This comes a day after BJP asked the Congress leader to defer the rally date from November 1 as it conincided with 1981 anti-Sikh riots anniversary.In a post on X, Rahul called for a “Save the Vote, Save the Country” march and mega rally, alleging that voter names had been deleted from electoral rolls and rules and laws violated."Our votes are being stolen, and we will not tolerate this quietly under any circumstances. Names have been removed from the voter lists. Rules and laws have been broken. And lathis have been used on those asking questions. Article Title: US asylum gamble blew gangster Himanshu Bhau’s cover: 'Used fake passport to evade global law'
Article Text:
Gangsters Himanshu Bhau (In black) and Neeraj Faridpuria in custody in US

Favourite route

‘Bhau used

fake passport

to evade global law’

Most-wanted gangster





NEW DELHI: A gamble to secure asylum in North America may have blown the cover of gangster Himanshu Bhau, one of north India’s notorious fugitives.A day after TOI reported his detention in Nevada, sources said a brief, staged detention in Feb by Bhau and his aide Neeraj Faridpuria, designed to exploit legal loopholes and claim asylum, backfired and unravelled the plan.The two face more than 25 criminal cases each across Delhi, Haryana and Punjab, including murder. Once the duo deliberately surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and details were fed into US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tracking system, which set off red flags.Sources said fugitives from India were aggressively seeking this modus operandi. Lawrence Bishnoi’s brother, Anmol, too had tried it but was busted.Currently lodged at the Henderson Detention Center under the jurisdiction of ICE, Bhau, sources said, used a forged passport under the alias Himanshu Singroha and evaded global law enforcement for over four years.However, his calculated scheme to get himself deliberately detained along with his chief associate, Neeraj Faridpuria, who also was using a fake passport under the name Neeraj Kaushik, triggered their detention.Once the duo deliberat-ely surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and personal details were fed into the ICE track-ing system. Picking up critical leads from this database entry, Indian law enforcement agencies and US security counterparts dug deeper into the background of “Himanshu Singroha”.Through cross-verification with local intelligen-ce sources, police contacts, and diplomatic counterparts, authorities confirmed that the individual in custody was indeed the high-profile fu­gitive Himanshu Bhau, a source said.The details on the ICE portal, accessed by TOI, corroborate the details, including the fake name on the passport. Investigations further revealed Faridpuria also shifted his base from Portugal to the US in late 2025 before reuniting with Bhau.The cops shared a dossier, including a photograph showing Faridpuria with guns and their other biometric details, which confirmed they were using forged documents. They were formally detained and information was shared with Indian agencies.The two are linked to the 2024 murder in South Delhi’s Aya Nagar in which over 70 bullets were fired, another recent connected killing, the 2019 murder of Congress leader Vikas Chaudhary in Faridabad, and a shooting outside YouTuber Elvish Yadav’s residence.Following confirmation of their detention in a Nevada prison, Indian agencies are working with US auth­orities to expedite their deportation. A special team is likely to be dispatched to expedite deportation.
Article Summary: Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Faridpuria face more than 25 criminal cases each across Delhi, Haryana and Punjab, including murder. Once the duo deliberately surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and details were fed into US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tracking system.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $325 million KC Current extend historic unbeaten home run to 31 matches
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes (Getty Images)

Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current eye home playoff advantage

KC Current rely on Temwa Chawinga and Croix Bethune before Decision Day

The Kansas City Current have another postseason to prepare for, giving owners Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes another reason to celebrate their investment in women’s soccer. The club has secured its third consecutive National Women’s Soccer League playoff berth, overcoming a season of major changes to remain among the league’s contenders. However, qualification is only the first step. With home-field advantage still up for grabs, Kansas City faces an important final stretch that could shape its chances of making a deep postseason run.The Current officially secured their playoff place after the Portland Thorns defeated the North Carolina Courage 1-0 on Friday night, October 23. Kansas City, Utah Royals and Portland Thorns each have 47 points, placing the three clubs in the playoff picture.For Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes, who are part of the Current’s ownership group, the achievement reflects the club’s continued competitiveness despite a challenging campaign.Kansas City will host the Washington Spirit on Sunday, October 25, in its final home match of the regular season. The match carries extra importance because a victory could strengthen the Current’s chances of earning a top-four seed and hosting a playoff game.The club also hopes to welcome 18,000 supporters for its annual fan appreciation match, potentially setting another attendance record. Strong home support has been a defining feature of Kansas City’s season, with the team remaining unbeaten across 31 consecutive home matches, an NWSL record.Head coach Chris Armas has faced a demanding first season in charge of a women’s team. Roster changes and shifting availability have tested the squad, but the Current have continued to collect important results.Kansas City’s home form has helped offset its inconsistent results away from home. The team has recorded a 10-0-4 home record, compared with a 4-1-9 mark on the road.The Current have scored 50 goals this season, including 37 at home. Temwa Chawinga remains a major attacking threat, leading the team with 12 goals despite missing matches through injury and international duty.Croix Bethune has also made a significant impact. Her 10 assists have matched the NWSL single-season record, which she shares with Utah’s Cloé Lacasse.The next challenge will be maintaining that momentum when the regular season concludes. On Decision Day, November 1, Kansas City will face Racing Louisville, currently 15th in the standings. All 16 teams are scheduled to play at 4 p.m. Central Time.The NWSL playoffs begin with the quarterfinals from November 6 to 8. For the Mahomes-owned club, securing a favourable seed could provide a valuable advantage as it pursues another postseason run.
Article Summary: KC Current have secured their third consecutive National Women’s Soccer League playoff berth. Kansas City will host the Washington Spirit on Sunday, October 25, in its final home match of the regular season. The club has recorded a 10-0-4 home record, compared with a 4-1-9 mark on the road.

Article Title: ‘Saddam Hussein opened a cheesecake factory’: Obama’s jibe at Trump’s White House
Article Text:
‘Jawlines and testosterone’: Obama takes a dig at Hegseth amid Iran conflict

Obama targets Pete Hegseth

What are US midterm elections

Former US President Barack Obama took a dig at Donald Trump over his renovation plans for the White House, saying Trump has "got the White House looking like former Iraq President Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory".Obama made the remarks while campaigning for the midterm elections in Ohio. He mocked Trump’s changes to the White House, saying the president appeared more interested in renovations than other matters."I don't know if you've noticed, but he seems very focused on home renovations. He should be on HGTV. The guy’s building a ballroom that’s bigger than the White House. Paved over the Rose Garden, put a helicopter pad on the South Lawn, and there’s gold everywhere! What’s up with the gold? Everything—more gold!” Obama said.He continued his criticism, drawing laughter and applause from the crowd. “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. Just gold everywhere."After his speech, Obama took to social media platform X to urge voters to support Democratic candidates in Ohio’s gubernatorial and Senate elections."Ohio, let's do what we can to elect Amy Acton as your next Governor and Sherrod Brown as your next US Senator! They’ve dedicated their lives to fighting on behalf of all Ohioans," Obama wrote.Obama also stressed the importance of grassroots campaigning and high voter turnout, saying collective action could help bring about positive change in the country."If we’re willing to organise and mobilise, if we’re willing to turn out in big numbers in Ohio and across this country, if we’re willing to vote for change and vote for Democrats up and down the ballot, then this election might just mark the moment this country began moving in a better direction," he stated.He ended his message by urging voters to make sure they cast their ballots.Obama also criticised US defence secretary Pete Hegseth, linking the ongoing conflict with Iran to concerns over the country's military preparedness."Hundreds of Americans have been wounded. We have run down our stock of missiles, and Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, you’ve got the defense secretary who’s squarely focused on important matters like the jawlines and testosterone levels of our troops," he said.US midterm elections take place every four years, halfway through a president’s four-year term. They are seen as an important test of public opinion on the president and the ruling party.The elections determine control of Congress, with all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and roughly one-third of the Senate seats up for election. The results can influence the president’s ability to pass laws and implement policies.
Article Summary: Former US President Barack Obama took a dig at Donald Trump over his renovation plans for the White House. Obama made the remarks while campaigning for the midterm elections in Ohio. He also criticised US defence secretary Pete Hegseth, linking the ongoing conflict with Iran to concerns over the country's military preparedness.

A protester was hit in the leg by a tear gas shell and admitted to hospital. The East Siang district administration imposed restrictions on public gatherings and processions in Pasighat, Mebo and Ruksin, citing apprehensions of vandalism, arson and a potential breach of law and order following protests and bandh-related activities.In an executive order issued Saturday, deputy commissioner Jayanti Pertin said the restrictions would come into effect from 5pm on Oct 24 and remain in force until withdrawn or modified.The violence began after a 12-hour bandh called by Adi Baane Kebang United, along with other organisations, against the proposed project ended peacefully at 5pm. The bandh, however, was not observed in Pasighat area.One of our deputy SPs suffered a head injury and has been evacuated to Dibrugarh, where he is being treated.Central police force personnel were also badly hurt, Pasighat IGP (central range) Hibu Tamang said.The mob also pelted stones at a hospital where injured central force personnel had been taken. At least nine police vehicles were damaged. The groups dispersed around 4am.“A youth group calling itself ‘Gen Z’ suddenly emerged and sat on a dharna on the Mebo side. Around 2pm, this group entered Pasighat jurisdiction. They blocked the Pasighat-Boleng highway and did not let traffic pass. They had no clear demand. They said they would sit on a dharna indefinitely, and there was also slogan-shouting,” Tamang said.He said police and civil authorities persuaded the group to leave the highway for two hours without any result. “As darkness fell, the group became very violent and unruly. A violent mob of 200-300 began pelting stones at police and the magistrate. Some of them were carrying liquor and beer bottles in their hands and were intoxicated. Police handled it gently and did nothing other than using tear gas,” the IGP said.Police said that they documented the incident on video and photographs.Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu expressed concern and offered to meet the groups for talks.
Article Summary: Protests against Arunachal Pradesh's proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project turned violent at Pasighat, East Siang district, on Friday night. "Gen Z" protesters allegedly torched the NHPC office and a police station, and vandalised and looting the residences of two MLAs and the state BJP president. The violence continued in waves for nearly nine hours early Saturday, leaving "over 40 police personnel injured in stone-pelting"

Article Title: Sourav Ganguly vs 'Doosra': Delhi high court seeks filmmakers’ reply on personality rights plea, asks to arrange screening
Article Text:
The Delhi high court has ordered the makers of 'Doosra' to respond to Sourav Ganguly's plea





NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Friday asked the makers of the film "Doosra" to respond to cricketer Sourav Ganguly's plea alleging violation of his personality rights in the movie, which was released in theatres earlier in the day.A vacation bench of Justice Vinod Kumar said the question of granting interim relief against the film could be decided only after the defendants filed their replies.The court also asked them to arrange a screening of the movie, news agency PTI reported.Justice Kumar, who held court during the high court's Dussehra break, issued summons to the film's producers, director and distributor in the lawsuit filed by Ganguly and Luv Films LLP, which is producing a biopic of the former India captain.The senior counsel representing the defendants submitted that "Doosra" was not a biopic but a fictional story about a middle-class girl from Rajasthan who is inspired by certain sporting events involving Ganguly."(The defendants to make) arrangements for playing the film so that it can be decided whether the personality rights of the plaintiff are violated or not," the court said, listing the matter for hearing on October 29.The defendants' counsel argued that the plea seeking interim relief had become infructuous as the film had already been released. However, the complainant' lawyer contended that a stay could still be granted, PTI reported.On Thursday, the high court had refused to stop the theatrical release of "Doosra" on Ganguly's plea.The senior counsel appearing for the filmmakers had assured the court that the film was not a biopic and that the necessary permissions had been obtained from the appropriate rights holders to use certain clips involving Ganguly.Ganguly's counsel apprehended a violation of the cricketer's personality rights, arguing that no licence had been obtained from him for the production of "Doosra".The defendants' counsel, however, contended that a player cannot claim "personality rights" over clips from the 2002 NatWest series."Doosra: India's Other Freedom Struggle" is a sports drama directed by Abhinay Deo and starring Plabita Borthakur, Ankur Vikal and Samidha Guru.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Delhi high court orders makers of 'Doosra' to respond to Sourav Ganguly's plea. Court also asks them to arrange a screening of the movie. Ganguly had filed a lawsuit alleging violation of his personality rights in movie. Court had refused to stop the theatrical release of " doosra" on Thursday.

Article Title: 'Told to post it': Delhi youth arrested in ex-CM Siddaramaiah sting clip case; Bengaluru court grants 22-year-old conditional bail
Article Text:
Accused Ritesh Pandey was granted conditional bail.

'Told to post clips'





BENGALURU: Sleuths from the Central Crime Branch (CCB), Bengaluru, picked up a 22-year-old man in Delhi late Friday night in connection with the alleged sting operation involving former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah , marking the first arrest in the case. He was brought to Bengaluru early Saturday morning and produced in court.A local court granted accused Ritesh Pandey conditional bail, directing him to inform the police before leaving Bengaluru and appear for questioning whenever summoned.Police sources said Pandey uploaded the contentious video on multiple social media platforms, including a YouTube channel named ‘Karnataka Honeytrap’.He allegedly told investigators that Prajwal Prasad, a member of a political party’s social media wing, had instructed him to upload the clip.According to an investigating officer, Pandey bought a used Android phone for Rs 15,000 from a shop in Delhi’s Karol Bagh market and used a USB device to upload the video. Police have recovered CCTV footage showing him buying the phone and seized a copy of the purchase bill, the officer added.Police have also issued notices to two members of a political party’s social media team, Mohan Gowda and Chandan, seeking information about who supplied the video to Pandey. Both have been unresponsive, police sources said.A senior IPS officer said investigators had questioned those connected with the case, including people who appeared or were heard in the video.
Article Summary: Sleuths from the Central Crime Branch (CCB), Bengaluru, picked up a 22-year-old man in Delhi late Friday night in connection with the alleged sting operation involving former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah. He was brought to Bengaluru early Saturday morning and produced in court. Accused Ritesh Pandey was granted conditional bail.

Article Title: How Bengaluru advocate’s death turned into a murder probe: 'Fight over auto fare, suspected heart attack, then a post-mortem twist'
Article Text:
Police have taken Pruthviraj Appajigowda into custody.

Found unconscious on Outer Ring Road

Argument over fare allegedly led to assault

Missing phone, cash allegations under probe





BENAGLURU: An argument over an auto-rickshaw fare, a suspected heart attack and a post-mortem twist have turned the case of a 43-year-old Bengaluru advocate into a murder probe.Police have taken Pruthviraj Appajigowda, 31, an auto-rickshaw driver from Gollarahatti on Magadi Road, into custody in connection with the death of Sri Ram, a resident of Kengunte.Investigators are also looking for other auto drivers who were allegedly present during the confrontation.Sri Ram was found unconscious on Nagarabavi Outer Ring Road on the morning of October 9. Hoysala police personnel on patrol rushed him to a nearby private hospital, where he died later that day.Initially, his death was suspected to be due to a heart attack. However, his family noticed injury marks on his body and approached Annapoorneshwarinagar police, suspecting foul play.The body was sent for a post-mortem examination. The report, which arrived recently, indicated that the advocate had died due to a blood clot in the brain, prompting investigators to look into the circumstances surrounding his death.The investigation led police to Pruthviraj, who allegedly attacked Sri Ram near Ambedkar Institute of Technology in Mallathahalli.According to an investigating officer, Sri Ram had asked Pruthviraj for a ride but disagreed with the fare quoted by the driver. He then walked away, saying he would take another auto-rickshaw. Pruthviraj allegedly followed him and attacked him, pushing him to the ground and causing internal head injuries.“There was a heated argument between the two over the tariff. Sri Ram had asked Pruthviraj for a ride and did not agree to the price quoted by him. Saying he will catch another auto, Sri Ram walked away. Angered over the refusal, Pruthviraj followed him and attacked. Sri Ram sustained internal head injuries when Pruthviraj pushed him to the ground. There were few more auto drivers with Pruthviraj when the incident took place and we are looking for them,” an investigating officer said.Police subsequently traced the auto-rickshaw and its driver, leading to Pruthviraj being taken into custody.Investigators are also examining allegations that Sri Ram’s mobile phone and some cash went missing after the incident.“There are allegations that accused person had taken away Sri Ram’s mobile phone and some cash. We are looking into it,” the officer added.Police are searching for the other auto-rickshaw drivers allegedly present during the confrontation as they investigate the circumstances leading to the advocate’s death.
Article Summary: Police have taken Pruthviraj Appajigowda, 31, into custody in connection with the death of Sri Ram, a resident of Kengunte. Sri Ram was found unconscious on Nagarabavi Outer Ring Road on the morning of October 9. Police are searching for other auto drivers allegedly present during the confrontation.

Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces another planning hurdle

Travis Kelce’s landscaping plans spark wider neighborhood concerns

Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion has become the centre of a growing neighborhood dispute, with concerns about privacy, property boundaries and the look of the lakefront estate complicating his plans. Officials also placed conditions on parts of the front landscaping, leaving the project with more work to complete before the estate’s outdoor plans can move forward.Kelce’s property in Bratenahl, near Cleveland, spans approximately 21,000 square feet and includes eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, a guest cottage, a swimming pool and a converted ballroom and game room. Residents raised concerns about its appearance, its potential effect on wildlife and whether it would provide meaningful protection from unwanted attention. One neighbor warned that deer could become trapped on the fence’s pointed tops.The review process has highlighted the challenge of balancing a high-profile homeowner’s security needs with local rules designed to protect lake views, neighborhood character and property values.Sewer infrastructure remains one of the concerns raised by neighboring residents, but it is not the only issue holding up the project.Katherine Bolton, who has lived next door for 35 years, questioned plans to plant around 50 evergreen trees near an old clay sewer line. She said the roots could cause serious damage and cited a potential $75,000 repair bill for lining the pipe.“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure, and catastrophic sewage backups,” she said, citing AI-based research.Kelce’s construction team has pushed back by pointing to changes made in response to residents’ complaints. Project representative Jacob Kutz said the owners had already paid $7,500 to repair a damaged section of the sewer line without seeking contributions from the neighbors.The team also moved the fence two feet inside the property boundary, added access gates and paid to trim trees on neighboring land.Those adjustments have not resolved every disagreement. The board has allowed some landscaping work but wants a revised proposal for the shoreline trees.For Kelce, the next step is to return with a plan that addresses the remaining objections while meeting the village’s requirements. Concerns about privacy, property boundaries and the look of the lakefront estate complicating his plans. The Kansas City Chiefs star has faced fresh resistance from residents in Bratenahl.

Article Title: Bihar MLC polls: 5.32 lakh voters to decide fate of 150 candidates across 8 seats, JD(U) rift adds intrigue
Article Text:
Polling began at 8 am today for eight seats in the Bihar Legislative Council (Representative image)





PATNA: Polling for biennial elections to eight Bihar Legislative Council seats began at 8 am on Friday amid tight security, with 5.32 lakh voters eligible to decide the fate of 150 candidates, officials said.Voting will continue till 4 pm for four Graduates and four Teachers constituencies, they said.The combined electorate stands at 5,32,847, including 1,46,611 women and 37 third-gender voters, across 933 polling stations. Counting of votes will take place on October 27.The contest in the Patna Graduates constituency has drawn attention following an open rift within the JD(U), with Mokama MLA Anant Singh backing Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh against his own party's nominee, Neeraj Kumar.Kumar, a former minister and a close aide of former chief minister Nitish Kumar, is seeking a fourth consecutive term from the seat.Anant Singh has extended support to Anuj Singh, alleging that Neeraj Kumar had worked against him during last year's assembly elections.Apart from Patna Graduates, the other constituencies going to polls are Darbhanga Graduates, Tirhut Graduates, Kosi Graduates, Patna Teachers, Darbhanga Teachers, Tirhut Teachers and Saran Teachers.The terms of the sitting MLCs are due to expire on November 16.The BJP has fielded candidates in four constituencies, including three sitting MLCs seeking re-election, while the JD(U) has nominated candidates for the remaining four seats.The BJP nominees are MLCs Nawal Kishor Yadav, NK Yadav and Sarvesh Kumar, who are seeking re-election from Patna Teachers, Kosi Graduates and Tirhut Graduates, respectively.The party has also fielded Narendra Kumar Singh from Tirhut Teachers, a seat currently held by Sanjay Kumar Singh of the CPI, a constituent of the opposition INDIA bloc.The Jan Suraaj Party (JSP), led by Prashant Kishor, is contesting all eight seats. The party revised its candidate list after its initial announcement, replacing Bhushan Jha with Shyam Nandan Yadav in Tirhut Teachers and Ravindra Yadav with Mohammad Imtiyaz (Noorani) in Darbhanga Graduates.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Voting will continue till 4 pm for four Graduates and four Teachers constituencies. The combined electorate stands at 5,32,847, including 1,46,611 women and 37 third-gender voters. Counting of votes will take place on October 27.

Article Title: Farooq Abdullah's comments on Pakistan and Kashmir draw flak

SRINAGAR: National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah on Saturday declared that Pakistan had “saved” Kashmiris by keeping the issue alive at international forums, while being careful to say that “otherwise their (Pakistan’s) intentions are not good”.His statement drew flak from BJP, which slammed it as “seditious and anti-national”.“If you do not remain (committed to NC), you will be erased. Even our identity will disappear. Nothing will be left. They are silent today because there is noise in the world and our neighbour is constantly behind it. Everywhere they say ‘the decision regarding Kashmir has not been made’. That is what is saving us…,” Farooq told a meeting of NC workers in Baramulla. The words “they” and “their” were seen as an allusion to the Centre.Farooq’s son, J&K chief minister Omar Abdullah, had not reacted to his father’s remarks till late Saturday.Farooq urged NC workers and legislators to remain loyal to the party, whether in power or not, as he touched on a range of issues in his speech. “Hold on to the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you remain truthful and stand up for what is right, your future will never be secure,” the veteran said.Citing the 1947 tribal invasion, Farooq condemned the “atrocities” inflicted on Kashmiris by the raiders from Pakistan”. He paid tributes to Maqbool Sherwani, an NC worker who died staving off the intruders, saying his “sacrifice helped stop the raiders in Baramulla and save Kashmir”.Farooq also mentioned the Chittisinghpura massacre in which 36 Sikhs were killed in south Kashmir on March 20, 2000, during then US President Bill Clinton’s visit to India. He said a subsequent judicial inquiry had found that five men accused of carrying out the killings were not the perpetrators but shopkeepers “who had been picked up by police and killed”. According to Farooq, the inquiry judge should have investigated the massacre itself but was “told from Delhi” not to.BJP decried Farooq’s comments. Party functionary Ravinder Raina called them “treason” and asked how Pakistan could ever be a well-wisher of the people of J&K. “Farooq Abdullah chose Baramulla for his pro-Pakistan remarks just two days after the anniversary of Pakistan’s Oct 22, 1947 invasion of J&K. This is the land of Maqbool Sherwani, who stood against invaders, not a stage to whitewash Pakistan’s bloody history,” J&K BJP spokesman Sajid Yousuf Shah said.Peoples Conference’s Imran Reza Ansari cautioned against following Farooq. “If a common Kashmiri speaks in a similar tone, govt will in seconds put that person in detention under PSA or UAPA. Please save your children and your families. Don’t emulate this person,” Ansari said.
Article Summary: Farooq Abdullah said Pakistan had “saved” Kashmiris by keeping the issue alive at international forums. His statement drew flak from BJP, which slammed it as ‘seditious and anti-national’ “If you do not remain (committed to NC), you will be erased. Even our identity will disappear. Nothing will be left,” he said.

Article Title: No EC nod needed for voter to sue candidate over false information: Supreme Court
Article Text:
The Supreme Court said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A voter can now not only cast a vote in an election but can also drag an election candidate to court and initiate criminal proceedings for lying and furnishing a false declaration as Supreme Court has ruled that a complaint filed by a private person alleging an offence under Section 125-A of Representation of People Act (filing false affidavit) is maintainable and the Election Commission’s nod was not needed.Explaining the interplay between Section 125-A of Representation of People Act and Section 195(1) of the CrPC which says that no court shall take cognisance of any offences punishable under sections 172 to 188, including the offence of furnishing false information to a public servant, the top court held that Section 125A of RoP Act does not come within the ambit of Section 195 of CrPC and a court can take cognisance of a private complaint. The court’s ruling will further empower the electorate against candidates who lied in their affidavits.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the Karnataka HC order which had held that “right given to the voter is only to file an election petition, and not to register a private complaint of crime which is the duty of the Election Commission, if it wants to do so”.SC said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002, while Section 195 of CrPC was amended in 2006, and that the omission of the legislature to include Section 125-A of the RoP Act in Section 195 of CrPC was deliberate and no court would be barred from taking cognisance of an alleged offence under Section 125-A of the RoP Act, even on the complaint lodged by a private person.“Should we read into Section 195 of CrPC a prohibition in respect of Section 125-A of the RoP Act also, apart from those expressly included? If indeed it were the intention of the legislature that cognisance of any offence relating to furnishing of false information by a candidate in an affidavit with intent of being elected in an election (referred to in Section 125-A of the RoP Act) could only be taken if the complainant were a public servant, the same could have been provided by an amendment of Section 195, CrPC since Section 125-A of the RoP Act is of fairly recent origin. ”SC also refused to give credence to the EC’s press note that it can take cognisance of such complaints and refer such matters to the relevant investigating authorities on a case-to-case basis. “...Even though the ECI is supreme in its own sphere and has, indeed, issued guidelines/press notes based on its understanding of the statutory provisions, interpretation of statutes is primarily the task of the courts and such guidelines/press notes do not bind us,” the court said.It said that Karnataka HC erred in holding that a private complaint cannot be filed for an offence under Section 125A of RoP Act which is punishable up to six months of jail term. The HC had interpreted the provision solely upon reading the letter issued by the Election Commission of India on the issue which was rejected by the apex court.Allaying the apprehension that allowing the lodging of a criminal complaint by a private person would be misused and frivolous cases would be filed by political rivals, SC said, “If at all a complaint is lodged to harass an elected candidate or frivolous allegations are levelled therein, the laws of the country duly empower the competent magistrates to pass such order(s) as they deem fit and proper commensurate with the facts and circumstances of each case. ”
Article Summary: Supreme Court has ruled that a complaint filed by a private person alleging an offence under Section 125-A of Representation of People Act (filing false affidavit) is maintainable. The court’s ruling will further empower the electorate against candidates who lied in their affidavits.

Article Title: ‘Act of treason’: BJP slams Farooq Abdullah over claim 'Pakistan is protecting Kashmiris'
Article Text:
BJP accused Farooq Abdullah of echoing Pakistan's narrative and questioned his comments on the country's role in Jammu and Kashmir.

BJP condemns Farooq Abdullah's statement

JD(U) questions echoing Pak's narrative

VHP calls Kashmir integral part of India

Congress disagrees with Abdullah, raises statehood issue

What did Farooq Abdullah say

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Saturday strongly criticised National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah's remark claiming Pakistan was “protecting” the people of Jammu and Kashmir by repeatedly raising the " Kashmir issue " at international forums. BJP leaders accused Abdullah of echoing Pakistan's narrative.BJP Jammu and Kashmir leader Ravinder Raina called his remarks an “act of treason” and questioned how Pakistan could be considered a well-wisher of Kashmiris. Raina termed Abdullah's statement “highly condemnable and unfortunate”, alleging that Pakistan had supported terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir for decades.“The statement made by Dr Farooq Abdullah regarding Kashmir and Pakistan is highly condemnable and unfortunate. In fact, Dr Farooq Abdullah has committed an act of treason," Raina said."Pakistan is the killer of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. Over the last 35 years, Pakistan has sought to turn Jammu and Kashmir into a graveyard and a cremation ground. This is the very same Pakistan that has fostered terrorism within Jammu and Kashmir—providing training, bombs, guns, pistols, ammunition, and grenades to terrorists. How could Pakistan ever be a well-wisher to the people of Jammu and Kashmir?" he added.Uttar Pradesh minister Suresh Kumar Khanna also accused Abdullah of exploiting Kashmiris throughout his political career. He said the region's integration into the national mainstream under the Modi government was in the best interests of its people.“It is people like Farooq Abdullah who have exploited Kashmir throughout their lives. Farooq Abdullah is responsible for reducing Kashmiris to second-class citizens, and he ought not to be making such statements. It is precisely because of India’s diversity that Kashmir is now integrated into the nation’s mainstream, and every citizen of Kashmir enjoys the same rights as those in the rest of India. Therefore, the current situation in Kashmir—brought about by the Modi government—is what is truly in the best interest of the Kashmiri people. Today, the people of Kashmir are at their happiest, thanks to the Modi government,” Khanna said.BJP leader Altaf Thakur also condemned Abdullah's remarks, calling them an attack on India's unity and integrity. He demanded action against the National Conference chief.“This is an open rebellion against the country. His statement is against the unity and integrity of the country. The National Conference has always been anti-country. The statement made by Farooq Abdullah is completely an anti-country statement. Action should be taken against him,” Thakur said.Chhattisgarh deputy chief minister Vijay Sharma questioned Abdullah's allegations about the Centre's intentions towards Jammu and Kashmir, asking whether he considered himself separate from India.“If we point out that they lack love for the country, they immediately start complaining that such things are being said about them. He himself served as chief minister, and now his son is chief minister. He has full access to all resources—from across India and everywhere else. Yet, he still makes such accusations. If he claims that India’s intentions were not good, does that mean he views himself as separate from India? He should learn from his own son, Omar Abdullah,” Sharma said.Janata Dal (United) state president G M Shaheen also criticised Abdullah, questioning why he continued to echo Pakistan's narrative despite having held several constitutional positions.“When a leader like Farooq Abdullah makes such a statement and supports Pakistan, what else can I call it but a misfortune? He has served as a chief minister, a member of the Rajya Sabha, and a member of parliament; he has worked within the framework of the country’s Constitution, yet, he chooses to speak the language of Pakistan. It is truly shameful. If Jammu and Kashmir is safe, it is because of India. Why does he always echo Pakistan’s narrative? The militancy that has plagued Kashmir since the 1990s was, in part, a consequence of his government. Whenever these people have come to power, they have invariably begun to speak the language of Pakistan. This is nothing new for Farooq Abdullah, but the nation should hold him accountable,” Shaheen said.Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) leader Vinod Bansal also condemned Abdullah's comments, asserting that Jammu and Kashmir would always remain an integral part of India. He questioned the suggestion that Pakistan was protecting Kashmiris.“Kashmir was, is, and will always remain an integral part of India. They live in India and sing praises of Pakistan. Is Kashmir safe because of Pakistan, or is Kashmir safe by showing India's strength to Pakistan? If this is his statement, then there is no greater treason than this,” Bansal said.Congress leaders also disagreed with Abdullah's remarks about Pakistan but raised concerns about the political and administrative situation in Jammu and Kashmir, particularly the delay in restoring statehood.Congress leader Ravinder Sharma said Jammu and Kashmir was an integral part of India and accused Pakistan of promoting terrorism. Citing the Shimla Agreement, he argued that Pakistan had no right to raise the Kashmir issue. He also highlighted concerns about the treatment of minorities and the continued denial of statehood to the region.“Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India, and it will remain an integral part. Pakistan spreads terrorism. Pakistan has no right or claim to raise the issue of Jammu and Kashmir, especially following the Shimla Agreement, in which it was agreed in writing that bilateral issues would be addressed through direct, bilateral engagement. Thirdly, regarding Farooq Abdullah’s remarks: he pointed to the disenfranchisement of minority voters, the use of bulldozers against minorities, and other forms of oppression, noting that there is an elected government in Kashmir. The Congress party is also fighting for this, demanding to know why, despite repeated promises, an undertaking given to the Supreme Court, and discussions in Parliament, statehood is still being denied to the people of Jammu and Kashmir. In that context, we also recognise that the people of Jammu and Kashmir are facing oppression,” Sharma said.Congress leader Rashid Alvi also disagreed with Abdullah's position, pointing to the situation in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) while criticising the BJP government's handling of Jammu and Kashmir.“I do not agree with Farooq Abdullah on this. There is no doubt that the BJP government has committed excesses in Kashmir. But what is happening in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK)? People there regularly protest against the Pakistani government. If the people in PoK are unhappy and dissatisfied with the Pakistani government, what can Pakistan do about our Kashmir?” Alvi said.Abdullah said Pakistan's repeated efforts to raise the Kashmir issue internationally were putting pressure on India. He alleged that the Centre's intentions towards Jammu and Kashmir were not good and urged people to stand up for their rights.“What can you expect from Delhi? You must have the courage to stand up to them and fight. If you do not, you will be wiped out. Your name and identity will disappear, and no one will even remember you. Our neighbour is constantly after them. It goes everywhere, saying that the Kashmir issue has not been resolved. It is protecting us; otherwise, their intentions are not good. They say one thing but do something entirely different,” Abdullah said.He also called on people to stand by the truth, warning that their future would remain insecure unless they spoke out.“You must have the courage to stand by the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you speak the truth and stand firm by it, your future will never be secure,” he said.Apart from his comments on Pakistan and the Centre, Abdullah raised concerns about the mandatory two-year service requirement for doctors who pursue MBBS, MD or MS courses in Jammu and Kashmir. He alleged that a file related to the policy had been pending with the Lieutenant Governor for a year.“Doctors who come from outside Jammu and Kashmir to pursue MBBS, MD, or MS courses, as well as students who study medicine here, are required to serve for two years in villages, hospitals, and other areas across the region. If they fail to fulfil this requirement, they must pay Rs 50 Lakh to the administration. This is a region where a file has been pending with the Lieutenant Governor for a year, yet it has still not been approved. This is the state of affairs here. What can you expect from Delhi? Can you really expect them to deliver justice to you?” Abdullah said.
Article Summary: BJP leaders accused Abdullah of echoing Pakistan's narrative. BJP Jammu and Kashmir leader Ravinder Raina called his remarks an “act of treason” Uttar Pradesh minister Suresh Kumar Khanna accused him of exploiting Kashmiris throughout his political career.

Article Title: Defer Nov 1 rally, will hit festive business, traders urge Rahul; BJP raps Congress
Article Text:
CTI urged LoP Rahul Gandhi to postpone Congress’s Nov 1 rally.

CEC’s ‘impeachment’ on Oct 30

Nov 1 rally by Rahul to hurt Sikhs: BJP

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi’s Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged LoP Rahul Gandhi to postpone Congress’s Nov 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan until after Nov 10, citing business disruptions during the peak Diwali shopping season. CTI said the rally could affect market access and traffic for three to four days, potentially impacting Rs 10,000 crore in festive trade.CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said Delhi records Rs 25,000 crore in business on Dhanteras across major sectors. CTI claimed that traders suffered losses of Rs 3,000 crore in Oct due to rallies and road closures in Connaught Place, India Gate and central Delhi.INDIA bloc leaders will hold a “public impeachment” of CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Oct 30 and announce a public verdict. Article Title: Why do some women become the strongest defenders of patriarchy
Article Text:
Delhi University women took to streets demanding safety after news report of a gangrape near a girls college.

“Sir, let me say that I am not a feminist. I consider myself as a human being. As a human being we feel that it is our duty to help women, minorities, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, and also the neglected class.” Mamata Banerjee in Lok Sabha on Women’s Day, 2008.

Oxford dictionary defines

feminism

as 'the belief and aim that women should have the same rights and opportunities as men or the struggle to achieve this aim.'

Why do some women keep patriarchy alive

Azaadi

Oxford dictionary defines patriarchy as '​a society, system or country that is ruled or controlled by men.'

Is the 'aurat hi aurat ki dushman' concept real?

From 'mere sar mei dard hai, iska karan marrd hai' to 'ek sutta, 2 chai, marrd jaat haye haye', the protest saw viral slogans. (PTI image)

Can patriarchy give women a sense of power?

When tradition becomes a question of freedom

When women challenge the rules they grew up with

kutta nahi sher bano

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patriarchy gives some women a sense of belonging

Then why is it that some of us distance ourselves from this term? And why is it that some women uphold the very patriarchy that restricts them?A group called the NCMIndia Council for Men Affairs recently took out a 'Long Live Patriarchy' march that went viral on social media. The group also had women holding the banner. "In the name of equality, these girls don't want to do jhaadu-pocha, clean utensils or raise kids. They just want freedom, money and debauchery," one of the women at the march said. "Equality does not mean freedom to drink, smoke, roam around at night. Women are misusing their independence.does not mean shaming men."TOI spoke to Dolly Kumari, who is also a member of the group that actively raises men's issues, and asked her what patriarchy meant to her."Patriarchy cannot be understood simply as a system created by men to oppress women. When a woman speaks about men's issues, some people may find it surprising because they expect her to speak only from a particular gender-based perspective. But I do not believe empathy should have a gender. Supporting men who experience injustice does not mean denying the difficulties women face," she said."My objection is to the idea that everything traditional must be condemned as patriarchal and, therefore, bad. If a man wants to protect and provide for his family, and a woman willingly chooses to trust him in that role, why should society automatically call that oppression or brainwashed women?"It would appear, then, that women supporting patriarchy would be an anomaly. However, Dolly said that the purpose of their 'Long Live Patriarchy' initiative was to raise awareness of men's rights, which "we have been organising on Gandhi Jayanti for nearly a decade.""Equality should not become a competition between men and women. Women deserve justice, and so do men. We need a society where both can express their pain, seek support, and live with dignity without being judged by gender stereotypes," said Dolly."In the traditional Indian family, men were often expected to provide, protect and take responsibility for their families while women traditionally took on many responsibilities related to the home and children. These roles evolved within the social and economic realities of their time although it resulted in unequal rights and restrictions. Our history is not simply a story of oppression and therefore patriarchy should prevail. "Does different treatment of a son from daughter and parenting play a role in keeping misogyny alive? Or is this 'aurat hi aurat ki dushman hoti hai' syndrome.Devika Anand, a psychologist at Rise and Mind, believes that the answer lies partly in the way gender roles are normalised within families and communities."I think one way to understand this is that we don't always question the systems we grow up in, particularly when those systems are presented to us as normal, moral, or necessary. When a woman grows up learning that a good woman is one who sacrifices, adjusts, tolerates, or puts others before herself, these expectations can become deeply embedded in her understanding of what it means to be a woman," she said.Over time, these expectations may stop feeling like restrictions and start being seen as values. A woman may even derive a sense of identity or self-worth from having lived up to them, sometimes at considerable personal cost."When younger women choose differently, it can challenge not just her beliefs but also the meaning she has attached to her own sacrifices," Devika explained.This explains why some women who have experienced restrictions themselves may go on to impose similar expectations on younger women. Having spent years adjusting to restrictive norms, they may come to regard them as an inevitable part of life rather than something that can be challenged."There can also be a need to make sense of one's own experiences. If someone has made significant sacrifices because she believed there was no alternative, acknowledging that those sacrifices were unnecessary or unfair can be painful. It may bring up feelings of anger, grief, or regret. Believing that younger women must make similar sacrifices can sometimes help preserve the sense that those sacrifices had a purpose," Devika said.When certain expectations are repeatedly reinforced within families and communities, they can become the default way of relating to others. A woman may reproduce the same expectations she experienced, not necessarily because she wants younger women to suffer, but because she has learned to see those expectations as responsible or appropriate behaviour."Power doesn't always mean having equal power within a system. Sometimes, it means having more power than someone else within that system," Devika said.In a patriarchal family, a woman may have limited autonomy in relation to men but still hold considerable authority over younger women, daughters-in-law or other women in the household. She may have little influence over the rules themselves but gain status by enforcing them."This can give her a sense of belonging, security, or control in an environment where her own power is otherwise limited," Devika explained.There can also be a psychological incentive to conform. If a woman receives approval, respect or recognition for upholding family traditions, questioning those traditions may threaten not only her beliefs but also her position within the family or community.Calling kindness, compassion, empathy and nurture 'qualities' that women should have, Dolly said, "I feel that relationships are increasingly being discussed in terms of personal freedom, sometimes without equal emphasis on duties, compromise, commitment, and mutual accountability."Dolly believes that a woman does not have to reject tradition to prove that she is empowered. "I come from a traditional, patriarchal family, yet my father always encouraged me to participate in activities that people might traditionally associate with boys. I played sports, learned to ride a bike, built a career in technology, and today have a beautiful family of my own. Growing up with two brothers also gave me a personal experience of sharing opportunities and responsibilities across gender lines. That experience is one of the reasons I believe that having a traditional father or growing up in a strict household does not automatically mean being oppressed. Tradition and discipline are not inherently oppressive," she said.Devika, too, cautions against labelling every woman who holds a traditional belief as a victim of internalised misogyny, which may include judging women more harshly than men, policing other women's behaviour, or believing that women are inherently less capable or less deserving of autonomy.A 65-year old influencer from Haryana called Tai Savitri, who recently went viral over her commentary on society and patriarchy, told TOI that even though her experiences have been bitter, it was her educated children that taught her to become a feminist. "I was less educated. My kids got good education so I learnt a few things from them. It was also a feeling that I should do something for the women," she told TOI.She recalled facing criticism in her village, even though her family did not offer much resistance to her views."Yes, I have also heard that aurat hi aurat ki dushman hoti hai but I think it is more because of lack of education that pitied one woman against the other, a system wherein one woman was the slave of another. This created a scenario where women did not want other women to succeed in life," she said.In one of her viral videos, Savitri compared women who restrict other women to dogs that have become accustomed to living on a leash. "You must have seen dog owners taking their pets out. Even if they let go of this leash, by mistake or deliberately, you will notice that the dog itself will hold the leash in his mouth and give it back to his owner. Because the dog has now developed a habit of living like a slave and it has accepted its fate. It is the same with women who try to show other women in poor light. It is the same slave mentality. My only message to women is(don't be a dog, be a tiger). Whoever tries to put a leash on you or make you a slave, rip them to shreds," she said.There is a distinction between having a choice and the freedom to make that choice. Holding a traditional belief is not the same as denying another woman the right to choose differently. The consequences of that belief, and the degree to which it is imposed on others, matter.Women who defend patriarchal expectations are not necessarily motivated by a single cause. Their views may be shaped by the values they grew up with, the sacrifices they have made, the security they derive from their place within a family or community, or a genuine belief that traditional arrangements offer stability.The question, then, is not simply why some women become flagbearers of patriarchy. It is also why a system that can restrict women's choices sometimes offers them identity, belonging or authority in return—and what it would take for women to feel secure enough to question it.Perhaps the more useful question is not whether women are their own enemies, but whether a society that teaches women to measure their worth through sacrifice, obedience and conformity gives them enough room to imagine a different way of living.
Article Summary: A group called the NCMIndia Council for Men Affairs recently took out a 'Long Live Patriarchy' march that went viral on social media. The group also had women holding the banner. ToI spoke to Dolly Kumari, who is also a member of the group that actively raises men's issues, and asked what patriarchy meant to her.

NEW DELHI: From Tuesday (Oct 27), all railway passengers buying reserved tickets from reservation counters can opt for travel insurance. At present, optional travel insurance facility is available only for reserved tickets bought online.The insurance premium is only 45 paise per passenger, including taxes, with coverage of Rs 10 lakh in case of death and permanent total disability in a train accident.The scheme has provision for payment of Rs 7.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and up to Rs 2 lakh for hospitalisation expenses arising from injuries, as well as Rs 10,000 towards transportation of mortal remains of deceased passengers. The Railway Board has directed all its zones to implement the facility.It said, “Where a passenger opts for insurance, the applicable premium shall be collected along with the ticket fare through digital means only. Staff shall ensure that where the person is opting for insurance, payment is done through digital means.”Reservation staff will inform passengers about the availability of the optional insurance facility and facilitate the exercise of their choice.The board said reservation staff will ensure that the mobile number (mandatory) along with other requisite passenger particulars are captured accurately so as to facilitate transmission of relevant details to the insurance firm for issuance of the policy.Passengers opting for insurance shall be informed that the policy details will be communicated to their registered mobile number.It covers specified railway accidents and untoward incidents, including train collisions, derailments, violent attacks, robbery, arson and accidental falls from trains. Coverage extends to diverted routes and alternative transport arranged by the railways in certain cases of train diversion or short termination.Normal second class or general class passengers are not covered under the insurance policy. It is also not applicable to children below the age of 5 years for whom tickets are issued without a berth or seat. But it is applicable to children in 5-11 age group who have reservation with berth or without berth.
Article Summary: The insurance premium is only 45 paise per passenger, including taxes, with coverage of Rs 10 lakh in case of death and permanent total disability in a train accident. The scheme has provision for payment of Rs 7.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and up to Rs 2 lakh for hospitalisation expenses arising from injuries.

Article Title: Daughter’s inheritance rights can’t be defeated by limitation: J&K and Ladakh high court
Article Text:

JAMMU: The high court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh has restored a woman’s right to inherit her father’s property after a 44-year-long legal battle, holding that an adverse revenue entry recorded during when she was a minor cannot automatically defeat a legitimate inheritance claim on limitation grounds.The dispute dates back to Sept 14, 1982, when Themu, daughter of late Sonu, filed a civil suit claiming half share in land measuring 58 kanals and 11 marlas left behind by her father.She challenged mutation no. 43 dated Oct 15, 1966, which had been entered exclusively in favour of one Shib Devi and sought declaration of her inheritance rights along with consequential possession.On March 9, 2004, the sub-judge court in Kishtwar passed a decree recognising her entitlement. However, the district judge reversed the decree on Nov 7, 2012, primarily on the grounds of limitation and failure to establish paternity.Justice Shahzad Azeem of the HC, while allowing the appeal filed by Themu, set aside the judgment of the district judge, Kishtwar, observing that limitation cannot be determined on presumptions and conjectures, particularly where the claimant was a minor when her rights were initially disputed and the defendants failed to establish when the cause of action actually arose.

Article Title: Drug trafficking crackdown: Amit Shah hails Operation Trident; Rs 100 crore hawala transactions exposed, 18 arrested
